The big corporations are taking full advantage of all this job-killing technology, but they hardly ever pass those savings or technology down to the normal population.. Yes, in a way. We work jobs now because of two reasons: we need money to support ourselves, and we need to do something fulfilling with our time. As it is, jobs are by and large only marginally fulfilling. In an automated future, it would be wrong to demand that someone gets a job, but it would be the opposite to push them to find a productive way to spend their time. I think there will always be a place for manmade goods. Sure, you could buy a chair manufactured by a robot, but does it have as much value as a chair made by someone who put their time, energy, and creativity into a chair? That chair, made by human hands, is going to be unique. It's a individual. It stands out because someone decided to spend their personal resources on it. It would, theoretically, mean more to you because it connects you to the person that made it.

If jobs become an artifice of the past, then the only positive answer is to push people to create, learn, and discover for the sake of those efforts alone. It means that people who make your food aren't doing it because it's the best job they can find at the moment, but because they genuinely enjoy creating delicious meals that other people will enjoy. It means a carpenter doesn't build furniture or a home simply because they need the money, but because they take pleasure in the knowledge that they've created something that people will value and cherish.

That's my one brief moment of optimism for the day, I'm spent.
